title: Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal from Heritage Presbytery's judgment: the SJC answered the four issues yes, yes, no, and yes-but-not-reversible; it left the conviction on Charge 3 specifications 3.1, 3.2, and 3.4 and the indefinite suspension from office and the Lord's Supper in force. Charges 1, 2, and 4 and Charge 3 specification 3.3 had been dismissed below and were not reversed. No remand, reversal, or acquittal. The source header says “affirmed in part,” but the operative judgment granted no reversal or remand. Dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk; objection and protest filed but not adopted.
first_summary: An appeal challenged Heritage Presbytery's conviction of a minister for divisive behavior and indefinite suspension from office and the sacraments. The SJC affirmed in part: the charge was lawful, his public letters after the session acted were divisive, the censure was not unjust absent repentance, and there were process errors but no reversible error. A dissent argued the divisive-behavior charge was not provable from Scripture under BCO 29-1.
summary: An appeal challenged a presbytery's conviction of a minister for divisive behavior and its indefinite suspension from office and the sacraments. The SJC affirmed: the charge was lawful because publicly publishing disagreement with the session after it acted violated his ordination vows to subjection and peace/unity, even though “divisive” is not a constitutional term; the censure was not unjust absent repentance; procedural errors did not require reversal or remand. A dissent argued the charge failed BCO 29-1’s Scripture-proof requirement.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC held the charge lawful, behavior divisive, censure not unjust, and process errors non-reversible. Lines 185–193. Reasoning: ordination vows BCO 21-5 were violated by publishing disagreement after Session acted; impenitence made indefinite suspension appropriate under BCO 30-3; procedural issues were moot or non-prejudicial. Lines 197–268.

Objection by TE Gordon and protest also challenge the majority but were not adopted. Lines 387–596, 600–844. Source header says 'affirmed in part' at line 3, but the operative judgment grants no reversal or remand.
